The alternating current produced by the generator is connected to the primary coil of the ideal transformer in Figure B. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure A is a schematic diagram of the principle of a generator; in Figure B, the output terminal of the generator is connected to the primary coil of an ideal transformer, and a voltmeter V and a resistor R are connected in parallel across the two ends of the secondary coil; Figure C is a sinusoidal alternating-current graph of the output voltage u changing with time t, with the vertical axis marking a maximum value of about +311 V and a minimum value of about -311 V. The problem statement gives that the ratio of the numbers of turns of the primary and secondary coils of the ideal transformer is n1:n2=22:1. Reasoning: From Figure C, read that the maximum value of the generator output alternating voltage is Um=311 V. The resistance of the generator coil is negligible, so the effective value of the voltage applied to the primary coil of the transformer is U1=Um/√2=311/√2≈220 V. An ideal transformer satisfies U1:U2=n1:n2=22:1, therefore the effective voltage across the two ends of the secondary coil is U2=U1/22=220/22=10 V. In Figure B, the voltmeter is connected in parallel across the two ends of the secondary coil, and the voltmeter measures the effective value, so the reading is 10 V.
